title: FIXED_180D_DECAY_IS_TOO_STUBBORN_TUNE_IT
finding: Ant research (Deneubourg double-bridge; Jackson 2006 Pharaoh's ant) shows evaporation/decay is ESSENTIAL for convergence. Without it, early trails persist forever and the system can't adapt. Decay must be TUNED: too high = forgetful/revert-to-random; too low = stubborn/early trails persist even if suboptimal.
our_current_state: All our PheTrail NEGATIVE_TRAILS use a FIXED decay_days=180 (L-PHE-2). This is a fixed, possibly-too-STUBBORN rate. Early negative trails persist 180 days regardless of merit.
proposed_fix: Modulate decay by intensity (-10..+10). Higher intensity (operator 'known-immediately', 10) = longer persistence. Lower intensity = faster evaporation. This matches the ant model: reinforcement frequency + strength sets persistence, not a flat constant.
source: Deneubourg et al. double-bridge foraging (capabilitygraph.com); Jackson, Current Biology 2006 S0960-9822(06)01834-3 (Pharaoh's ant 3-pheromone, evaporation essential).

negative_trails.failure: Use fixed decay_days=180 for all pheromones regardless of intensity/merit.
negative_trails.root_cause: L-PHE-2 hardcoded 180d without tuning. Ant model shows fixed decay prevents convergence.

positive_trails.action: Decay rate = f(intensity -10..+10). 10=longest persistence, low=intent. Reinforcement sets persistence like ants.
positive_trails.verification: Ant evaporation research, Jackson 2006 + Deneubourg model.
